pathway.title: VSE CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings momentum is the main support for creditors, and part of it is organic. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.81% in Q3 against 16.74% a year earlier, organic revenue growth was about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026, and management raised revenue and margin guidance in both August and November. PAG supplied 32.10% of Q3 revenue and only about five months of it are in trailing results, so much of the scale gain is bought rather than earned. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C20; calculation C23

Leverage has almost doubled, and the evidence supports a range of 2.98x to 3.38x rather than management's 2.3x. Net debt rose from USD 223.4 million at year-end 2025 to USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30, before the Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05, whose pro forma effect is not established, and net leverage went from 1.74x to 3.38x on reported EBITDA. The 2.3x depends on USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes. The fall in issuer-stated net leverage from 3.6x at 2026-06-30 to 3.0x came from trailing Adjusted EBITDA rising USD 59.8 million as PAG quarters replaced earlier ones, not from lower debt: net debt rose USD 22.6 million in Q3 while the USD 64.1 million Atech purchase absorbed the USD 46.6 million of free cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C28

Cash conversion is the weakest part of the profile. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months 2026 and USD 27.5 million over the last twelve months, 9.14% of Adjusted EBITDA, because inventory took USD 148.4 million of cash, including stock for a new OEM auxiliary power unit programme. Q3 free cash flow of USD 46.6 million was 43.50% of Adjusted EBITDA and shows what better conversion looks like, but it is one quarter, and management gives no fourth-quarter figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

Liquidity and the maturity profile protect creditors for the next two years. Cash of USD 65.8 million and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million give USD 545.0 million, which is 6.03x the USD 90.4 million of 2027 scheduled principal and estimated interest, and 85.97% of principal is not due until 2033; the revolver matures in 2030, so no facility expires within twelve months. The only covenant evidence is a statement of compliance with a maximum net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio, so how much of the revolver is usable under stress is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vsec-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C18

Asset quality is the main concern for recovery. Goodwill and intangibles are 62.59% of assets and 94.01% of equity, tangible equity is USD 178.7 million, and inventory is 19.93% of assets after the auditor named slow-moving inventory write-downs a critical audit matter. Tangible assets of USD 1,676.0 million cover debt principal 1.71x on book value, but much of that cover is inventory and receivables whose value under stress is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; calculation C17; calculation C16

Margins have widened in both revenue types, which supports durability, but the record is short and was made in an upturn. Revenue less cost of products was 19.00% in nine months against 15.84%, and revenue less cost of services 14.86% against 10.10%, as repair rose to 58.78% of Q3 revenue. Management credits higher-margin engine products and repair, OEM licensed sales and acquisition synergies, and the margin of PAG itself is not itemized, so how much of the gain lasts through a downturn is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C27

Financial policy is acquisitive but equity-led, which is the best governance evidence available. About USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units funded most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, dividends were 3.20% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA and the only share repurchases are shares withheld for employee taxes, but six businesses were bought in 17 months and the PAG earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million can be paid in cash or equity at the issuer's choice. The proxy statement that would show board and ownership terms is not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C21; calculation C30

Guidance is credible on margin but implies a softer fourth quarter than the third. Full-year revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 520.5 million to USD 537.2 million, which is 0.70% to 3.78% below Q3 even though purchases closed in August and October add a fuller quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 98.2 million to USD 105.1 million against USD 107.2 million in Q3. Either the guide is conservative or demand is easing, and the fourth quarter is the nearest test of the view. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C23

runs.text: The credit's first strength is an equity-funded balance sheet. About USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units funded most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, so debt rose USD 667.1 million rather than by the full purchase price. That limits the leverage creditors carry for an acquisition that doubled revenue, and it shows equity markets will fund VSE's growth, which is a source of stress support. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

The second strength is near-term liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 545.0 million covers 2027 scheduled principal and estimated interest 6.03x, and 85.97% of principal falls due in 2033, so a refinancing event is not a risk for several years and the revolver is only 4.00% drawn. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C18

The third strength is earnings momentum with credible margin support. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 16.45% in FY2025 to 19.81% in Q3, and organic growth held at about 14% to 17% in each 2026 quarter, so earnings power per unit of revenue has improved while the business grew. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C23

The first weakness is leverage that depends on the EBITDA definition. Net leverage is 2.98x to 3.38x on defined earnings and 2.3x only with USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes, so an unverified add-back is doing much of the work in the headline ratio and a lender cannot test the covenant ratio that governs the facility. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1; calculation C4

The second weakness is cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months and 9.14% of Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months because inventory took USD 148.4 million of cash, so earnings do not yet reduce debt and deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and a fourth-quarter release of cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

The third weakness is an intangible-heavy asset base. Goodwill and intangibles are 62.59% of assets and tangible equity is USD 178.7 million, so a write-down after the preliminary purchase price allocations are finalized would cut equity without adding cash, and recovery value would rest on inventory and receivables whose value under stress is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C17

The fourth weakness is exposure to one customer group and to OEM agreements. The group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and the OEM agreements underpin distribution revenue and inventory value, so a single decision by a counterparty could remove revenue while leased facilities and inventory carrying costs stay. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C22

runs.text: The PAG acquisition closed on 2026-05-05 with purchase consideration of USD 2,020.0 million, made up of cash net of cash acquired of USD 1.75 billion, equity in a VSE subsidiary and an earn-out of up to USD 125.000 million recorded at fair value. The headline of about USD 2.025 billion in the annual report and releases is a different definition of the same price. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C12

Funding came in three layers. Common stock and tangible equity units raised about USD 1.3 billion in February 2026. The amended senior secured credit agreement added a USD 900.000 million term loan B due 2033-05-05, repaid the prior term loan and raised the revolver commitment from USD 400.000 million to USD 500.000 million due 2030-05-02. The tangible equity units also carry senior unsecured amortizing notes at 5.93% that amortize to 2029-02-01. Debt carrying value rose USD 667.1 million to USD 959.9 million by 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–29; calculation C10; calculation C11

Three smaller acquisitions bracket PAG: NorthStar on 2026-04-01 before it, and Atech on 2026-08-31, paid partly from the revolver, and Test Logic on 2026-10-05 after it; the Test Logic price is not stated and the deal is not in any period figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE CORP (issuer vsec), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module builds the financial foundation from the seven supplied filings and releases: statements for FY2024 to Q3 2026, net debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and the debt structure. The reporting entity is VSE Corporation and its subsidiaries, consolidated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose to USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 223.4 million at year-end 2025, so net leverage on reported EBITDA is now 3.38x rather than 1.74x and creditors carry a more levered, acquisition-driven credit than the FY2025 accounts show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C4; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratio depends on the denominator: 2.98x on management's adjusted EBITDA and 2.3x on its acquisition-adjusted measure, which adds pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes. Reported EBITDA holds only about five months of PAG, so 3.38x overstates run-rate leverage. Cash generation has not yet funded deleveraging: nine-month operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million after an inventory build of USD 148.4 million. Liquidity is USD 545.0 million of cash and undrawn revolver. The Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05 is not in these figures and its pro forma effect is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose USD 670.7 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The PAG purchase took about USD 1.75 billion of cash on 2026-05-05; equity and tangible equity unit proceeds of about USD 1.3 billion raised in February 2026 and a new USD 900.0 million term loan B paid for it, which is why debt carrying value rose USD 667.1 million while cash barely moved. Net debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 264.2 million went from 1.74x at FY2025 to 3.38x, and over the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 300.4 million it is 2.98x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C4; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios mean different things. Reported last-twelve-months EBITDA holds PAG only from 2026-05-05 while debt carries its whole financing, so 3.38x overstates run-rate leverage. The issuer's acquisition-adjusted EBITDA of USD 389.2 million adds USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes or audits, which is how management reaches 2.3x. The evidence supports a range, not one number, and the covenant ratio that governs the facility is defined differently again and its level is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash paid for interest was USD 26.8 million in FY2025 against reported EBITDA of USD 128.8 million, which is cover of 4.80x, up from 2.27x in FY2024 after the revolver was repaid from the Fleet sale proceeds and the October 2025 equity offering. No quarterly report states cash interest, and nine-month 2026 net interest expense of USD 17.9 million is flattered by interest income earned on cash held before the PAG closing. At the 2026-09-30 rates and balances, contractual interest on the term loan B, revolver and amortizing notes is about USD 57.7 million a year before swaps and fees, so reported EBITDA of USD 264.2 million would cover it about 4.58x. That is an estimate built from stated rates and balances, not a reported ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C11; calculation C20; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months 2026 after an inventory build of USD 148.4 million, and capital expenditure of USD 24.7 million left free cash flow at USD -3.4 million. The path improved within the year: operating cash flow was USD -34.7 million in the first half and USD 56.0 million in Q3 alone. Inventory is USD 893.0 million, 19.9% of total assets, and the FY2025 audit named the write-down of slow-moving inventory as a critical audit matter, so cash tied up in stock carries valuation risk that a creditor cannot see in the leverage ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 545.0 million, made up of USD 65.8 million of cash and USD 479.2 million of undrawn revolver commitments. The maturity profile is back-ended: the term loan B repays USD 9.0 million a year and the amortizing notes USD 23.7 million in 2027, but USD 841.5 million, 86.0% of principal, falls due at the 2033 term loan maturity. A current earn-out obligation of USD 27.4 million, most of it payable in cash or equity at the company's sole discretion, is a further possible claim on liquidity.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 27.1 million because management adds back acquisition and integration costs, stock-based compensation and a refinancing loss and deducts a non-cash earn-out gain; the add-backs are management's and are not independently verified. The acquisition consideration appears as a headline of about USD 2.025 billion, as purchase consideration that includes the earn-out at fair value, and as cash paid net of cash acquired; each is kept for its own use. Cash flow statements include discontinued operations for 2025 periods, so 2025 free cash flow does not match the continuing perimeter. Purchase price allocations for PAG, NorthStar and Atech are preliminary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for lower leverage is operating momentum: Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 107.2 million is the highest quarter on record and management guides FY2026 revenue growth of 65% to 66.5%. If the strong fourth-quarter cash generation that management expects is delivered and the pre-acquisition EBITDA is itemized, the 2.3x measure would be credible. If inventory keeps building without cash conversion, or the covenant levels leave little room, the reported 3.38x is the better guide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE CORP (issuer vsec), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the business, ownership, transaction history and governance evidence in the seven supplied sources. The reporting entity is VSE Corporation and its subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE is an acquisition-built aviation aftermarket company with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, so creditors rely on management's equity-funded acquisition record and PAG integration rather than owner support, and governance evidence is thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine-month 2026 revenue was USD 1,314.7 million, up 62.09%, and PAG supplied USD 278.2 million of it after closing on 2026-05-05. Equity and equity-linked units raised about USD 1.3 billion, which limited debt-funded growth, yet debt still rose to USD 959.9 million. One customer group was 20% of FY2025 revenue and inventory is USD 893.0 million. The proxy statement is not supplied, so board, ownership and pay facts are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C1; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a single-segment aviation aftermarket platform in which repair has overtaken distribution. Repair revenue was USD 318.0 million and distribution USD 223.0 million in Q3 2026, against distribution at 63.29% of FY2025 revenue, mainly because of the PAG acquisition. Customers are almost entirely commercial, with government customers at 1.10% of Q3 revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration is moderate but real. One affiliated customer group was 20% of FY2025 revenue and the United States was 56.61% and Canada 13.40%, so one relationship could remove a fifth of revenue while facility and inventory carrying costs stay. The 2026 reports do not update the customer share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C5; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is acquisition-led and funded with a high share of equity, which supports creditors, but integration is the main business risk. Six businesses were acquired between 2025-05-01 and 2026-10-05, including PAG at USD 2,020.0 million of purchase consideration, and about USD 1.3 billion of equity and equity-linked units covered most of the USD 1.75 billion cash price. Reported growth of 62.09% includes acquired revenue; pro forma growth as if PAG had been owned throughout 2025 was 22.81% and the issuer puts Q3 organic growth at about 17%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so stress support would have to come from public equity markets rather than an owner. The PAG seller will hold about 4.80% of the share count once its exchangeable subsidiary shares convert, automatically by 2029-05-05, and tangible equity unit holders receive shares from 2029-02-01; the sources state no board or veto rights for either, and the proxy statement that would show them is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsec-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is acquisitive but shareholder payouts are small. Dividends were USD 8.0 million in nine months 2026, 3.20% of Adjusted EBITDA, there were no repurchases beyond shares forfeited to cover employee taxes, and the credit agreement limits dividends annually, so leakage to equity is not the concern; repeated debt-supported deals are.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset quality depends on judgements a creditor cannot test. Inventory is 19.93% of total assets and goodwill and intangibles are 62.59%, the FY2025 audit named slow-moving inventory write-downs as a critical audit matter, and purchase price allocations for the acquired businesses remain preliminary, so a write-down would cut equity and earnings without adding cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance reporting is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control. The sources show regular quarterly reporting, effective disclosure controls and a fair-presentation audit opinion, while controls at four acquired businesses are still being integrated, and board composition, independence, ownership and pay are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the funding record: about USD 1.3 billion of equity and equity-linked units covered most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, no related-party fees, distributions beyond a small dividend or creditor-adverse actions appear in the sources, and the chief executive's disclosed sale plan covers about 0.12% of shares outstanding. A proxy statement that shows a holder with board or veto rights, a credit agreement with wide restricted-payment and investment baskets, or pre-acquisition earnings well below management's adjusted measure would push governance risk toward High. Disclosure of the acquired businesses' earnings that matches management's view and a clean fourth-quarter integration would move it toward Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsec-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no holder controls the company rests on the absence of any control disclosure in the filings and would change if the proxy shows a holder with board or veto rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement is not supplied, so the conclusion that financial policy is acquisitive but bounded is untested; wide restricted-payment, investment or unrestricted-subsidiary baskets would make it more adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - PAG's results before 2026-05-05 are available only as unaudited pro forma revenue and net income, so the underlying growth reading of 22.81% rests on an issuer-prepared pro forma; a materially different stand-alone history would change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is stated for FY2025 only, so the 20% share may be stale after PAG and Aero 3 broadened the base; a lower share would reduce the concentration conclusion and a higher one would sharpen it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report describes PAG as pending, so its risk factors predate the closing; the 2026 quarterly reports state no material change, which this module accepts as stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The PAG acquisition closed on 2026-05-05 with purchase consideration of USD 2,020.0 million, made up of cash net of cash acquired of USD 1.75 billion, equity in a VSE subsidiary and an earn-out of up to USD 125.000 million recorded at fair value. The headline of about USD 2.025 billion in the annual report and releases is a different definition of the same price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funding came in three layers. Common stock and tangible equity units raised about USD 1.3 billion in February 2026. The amended senior secured credit agreement added a USD 900.000 million term loan B due 2033-05-05, repaid the prior term loan and raised the revolver commitment from USD 400.000 million to USD 500.000 million due 2030-05-02. The tangible equity units also carry senior unsecured amortizing notes at 5.93% that amortize to 2029-02-01. Debt carrying value rose USD 667.1 million to USD 959.9 million by 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–29; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three smaller acquisitions bracket PAG: NorthStar on 2026-04-01 before it, and Atech on 2026-08-31, paid partly from the revolver, and Test Logic on 2026-10-05 after it; the Test Logic price is not stated and the deal is not in any period figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by an acquisition-led financial policy, because repeated deals raise integration and leverage risk, which implies a higher chance of leverage drifting up again. Countervailing evidence is the equity-funded financing and the absence of sponsor, related-party or distribution leakage. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium, with legal capacity and board control not established because the credit agreement and proxy statement are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Figures are USD as printed in the sources, converted from thousands to millions by exact division; percentages are shown to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rounded figures quoted in the findings:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: the proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting is not supplied, so board composition, independence, committee roles, compensation and beneficial ownership are not established; the control and alignment conclusions are bounded until it is obtained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: the executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the note indenture are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, investments, liens and unrestricted subsidiaries cannot be separated from willingness; the behaviour assessment is limited to documented actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: pre-acquisition earnings of PAG and the other acquired businesses are not itemized, so underlying growth and scale rest on an unaudited pro forma revenue and net income table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: customer concentration is not updated after FY2025, so the 20% customer group may be stale after PAG and Aero 3.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: the timing and form of the PAG earn-out payment are not stated, so the liquidity and dilution effect is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: whether any holder exercises control is not confirmed, because the filings contain no control disclosure and the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: the Test Logic purchase price is not stated and the acquisition is a subsequent event kept out of period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: revenue by geography is stated for FY2025 only, so the country shares may be stale; related-party transactions and fees are not captioned in the filings read, so their absence is not proof of none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE CORP (issuer vsec), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesizes the fundamental credit profile of VSE Corporation and its subsidiaries from the seven supplied sources and the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE is an adequate but newly levered credit: record earnings and USD 545.0 million of liquidity support creditors, while thin cash conversion and undisclosed covenant levels leave deleveraging dependent on a fourth quarter that management has only promised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30, before the Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05, whose pro forma effect is not established. Net leverage is 3.38x on reported EBITDA and 2.98x on Adjusted EBITDA, against management's 2.3x, which relies on earnings no filing itemizes. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months, and guidance implies fourth-quarter revenue below the third quarter. The primary downside path is weaker engine aftermarket demand stranding inventory of USD 893.0 million while debt stays fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C15; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings momentum is the main support for creditors, and part of it is organic. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.81% in Q3 against 16.74% a year earlier, organic revenue growth was about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026, and management raised revenue and margin guidance in both August and November. PAG supplied 32.10% of Q3 revenue and only about five months of it are in trailing results, so much of the scale gain is bought rather than earned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C20; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has almost doubled, and the evidence supports a range of 2.98x to 3.38x rather than management's 2.3x. Net debt rose from USD 223.4 million at year-end 2025 to USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30, before the Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05, whose pro forma effect is not established, and net leverage went from 1.74x to 3.38x on reported EBITDA. The 2.3x depends on USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes. The fall in issuer-stated net leverage from 3.6x at 2026-06-30 to 3.0x came from trailing Adjusted EBITDA rising USD 59.8 million as PAG quarters replaced earlier ones, not from lower debt: net debt rose USD 22.6 million in Q3 while the USD 64.1 million Atech purchase absorbed the USD 46.6 million of free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is the weakest part of the profile. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months 2026 and USD 27.5 million over the last twelve months, 9.14% of Adjusted EBITDA, because inventory took USD 148.4 million of cash, including stock for a new OEM auxiliary power unit programme. Q3 free cash flow of USD 46.6 million was 43.50% of Adjusted EBITDA and shows what better conversion looks like, but it is one quarter, and management gives no fourth-quarter figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile protect creditors for the next two years. Cash of USD 65.8 million and undrawn revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million give USD 545.0 million, which is 6.03x the USD 90.4 million of 2027 scheduled principal and estimated interest, and 85.97% of principal is not due until 2033; the revolver matures in 2030, so no facility expires within twelve months. The only covenant evidence is a statement of compliance with a maximum net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio, so how much of the revolver is usable under stress is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vsec-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset quality is the main concern for recovery. Goodwill and intangibles are 62.59% of assets and 94.01% of equity, tangible equity is USD 178.7 million, and inventory is 19.93% of assets after the auditor named slow-moving inventory write-downs a critical audit matter. Tangible assets of USD 1,676.0 million cover debt principal 1.71x on book value, but much of that cover is inventory and receivables whose value under stress is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; calculation C17; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have widened in both revenue types, which supports durability, but the record is short and was made in an upturn. Revenue less cost of products was 19.00% in nine months against 15.84%, and revenue less cost of services 14.86% against 10.10%, as repair rose to 58.78% of Q3 revenue. Management credits higher-margin engine products and repair, OEM licensed sales and acquisition synergies, and the margin of PAG itself is not itemized, so how much of the gain lasts through a downturn is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is acquisitive but equity-led, which is the best governance evidence available. About USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units funded most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, dividends were 3.20% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA and the only share repurchases are shares withheld for employee taxes, but six businesses were bought in 17 months and the PAG earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million can be paid in cash or equity at the issuer's choice. The proxy statement that would show board and ownership terms is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C21; calculation C30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Guidance is credible on margin but implies a softer fourth quarter than the third. Full-year revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 520.5 million to USD 537.2 million, which is 0.70% to 3.78% below Q3 even though purchases closed in August and October add a fuller quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 98.2 million to USD 105.1 million against USD 107.2 million in Q3. Either the guide is conservative or demand is easing, and the fourth quarter is the nearest test of the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that management's own measures show deleveraging: adjusted net leverage was 2.4x at 2026-06-30 and 2.3x at 2026-09-30, Q3 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million, margin guidance has been raised twice, and at the guided year-end Adjusted EBITDA a flat net debt would give 2.58x to 2.53x. If the fourth quarter delivers free cash flow that repays the revolver, if the pre-acquisition earnings are itemized and hold near USD 88.8 million, and if the covenant levels prove wide, the view would move toward a stronger business profile with adequate liquidity. It would turn weaker if fourth-quarter revenue falls below the guidance-implied USD 520.5 million, if inventory keeps building without cash conversion, or if the covenant levels sit close to current ratios; a 20% fall in Adjusted EBITDA alone, with net debt unchanged, would take net leverage to 3.72x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The margin and cash conversion judgements rest on about two quarters with PAG in the group and on an upturn in aviation demand, so a weak fourth quarter would lower both and a repeat of the Q3 record would raise them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE Corporation is a Delaware company based in Miramar, Florida, listed on NASDAQ, that distributes aviation aftermarket parts and repairs engine, auxiliary power unit, avionics and airframe components as one reportable segment. Its customers are almost entirely commercial: commercial customers were 98.51% of nine-month revenue, and repair has overtaken distribution at 58.78% of Q3 revenue. Revenue was USD 1,615.9 million over the last twelve months, 2.06x the FY2024 level, so the business has been rebuilt by acquisition since the Fleet and Federal and Defense sales. The credit consequence is that cash flow follows aircraft utilization and maintenance demand, and the scale that supports debt service was bought rather than proven through a full cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C27; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE has no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder. The PAG seller holds exchangeable subsidiary shares that become about 4.80% of the share count after exchange, and tangible equity unit holders receive shares from 2029. Stress support would therefore have to come from public equity markets rather than an owner, and the February 2026 raise of about USD 1.3 billion shows those markets were open to it. The term loan B and revolver are senior secured under a credit agreement to which subsidiaries are guarantors, while the amortizing notes of USD 61.0 million are senior unsecured, so 93.76% of debt principal ranks as secured. The guarantor list and collateral perimeter are not supplied, so structural seniority is not assessed here, and the proxy statement that would show board composition and holdings is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C30; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional aftermarket parts and repair work, and it is cyclical: the annual report states the aviation industry has been subject to downward cycles that lower demand for engine and component parts and repair and raise credit risk. Organic growth of about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026 was attributed to commercial engine aftermarket activity, newly awarded OEM distribution agreements and share gains, and the issuer holds exclusive manufacturing, distribution and repair rights over certain fuel control systems and PT6 fuel pumps. The risk is that distribution revenue rests on OEM agreements whose terms are not supplied, and one customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue, roughly USD 222.5 million, and the annual report warns that results would suffer if lost business could not be replaced in time on comparable terms while leases and inventory remain. Pricing power is not evidenced: the annual report lists inflation without contractual protection and tariffs as risks, and no price and volume split is disclosed. Creditors should treat revenue as demand-driven and moderately concentrated, with no contracted floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation C23; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The income statement does not separate fixed and variable cost, but the pattern points to meaningful operating leverage: revenue less cost of services rose from 10.10% to 14.86% in nine months as repair scale grew, and revenue less cost of products from 15.84% to 19.00%. Repair brings labour, certified facilities and capacity commitments, substantially all of the facilities are leased, and the annual report names skilled labour and inflation without contract protection as risks. The mechanism is that the same operating leverage works in reverse if volume falls, so margins are defensible in a moderate slowdown but not proven in a downturn. Reported EBITDA also moves with non-cash items: an earn-out fair value gain of USD 8.9 million sits in 2026 reported EBITDA against a charge of USD 29.2 million in nine months 2025, and management's add-backs lift nine-month Adjusted EBITDA USD 27.1 million over reported, so Adjusted EBITDA is the better trend measure but carries management's judgement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C5; calculation C24; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and is not what limits cash flow: capital expenditure was USD 31.5 million over the last twelve months, 1.95% of revenue, and the issuer does not split maintenance from growth spending, so capex flexibility cannot be separated from growth plans. Working capital is the drain: inventory rose USD 339.2 million since year-end to 55.26% of last-twelve-months revenue, with USD 148.4 million of cash purchases and USD 200.2 million acquired with PAG, and management ties the purchases to a new OEM auxiliary power unit programme and engine initiatives. Interest is the second claim: estimated contractual interest is USD 57.7 million a year before swaps and fees, and cash interest and cash taxes for 2026 are not stated, while FY2025 cash interest was USD 26.8 million and cash taxes USD 16.1 million. Two claims sit outside the debt figure: the earn-out liability of USD 27.4 million, which the issuer may settle in cash or equity, and long-term operating lease obligations of USD 75.8 million; the annual report says finance leases are not material, and the sources mention no pension, factoring or supply-chain finance obligation. Free cash flow was USD 46.6 million in Q3 and USD -50.0 million in the first half, so EBITDA is converting to cash unevenly, and deleveraging over the next four quarters will come mainly from EBITDA growth unless inventory growth stops.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C15; calculation C29; calculation C16; calculation C14; calculation C2; calculation C33; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry limits pricing power. The annual report describes a fragmented industry with intense competition, many competitors larger and better resourced than VSE, and OEMs and certified repair facilities that may bundle services. The consequence is that margin gains must come from mix and proprietary repair approvals rather than scale, which is how the third-quarter release frames the Atech purchase, with sole-source repairs on flight-critical parts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Entry barriers are clearest in repair. Certification and conformance are required before a part is installed, and repairs may be done only at certified facilities with certified technicians, which protects repair margins from new entrants, while the annual report names no comparable barrier for distribution beyond exclusive OEM rights whose duration is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is modest on the evidence supplied. The annual report names new aircraft components, advanced replacement parts and AI-optimized maintenance as ways competition could change, but shows no loss of volume, so this is a monitoring item and not a driver of the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power centres on concentration. Commercial airlines, MRO integrators and operators buy on availability, turnaround time and price, and one customer group of about 20% of FY2025 revenue could reduce orders or seek relief from its agreements; the 2026 reports do not update that share, so the effect of the PAG purchase on concentration is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C22; calculation C30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is material. VSE depends on OEM licences and distribution agreements, on third-party package delivery companies and on suppliers who may be disrupted by tariffs and supply chain delays, and OEMs are also competitors. A non-renewed OEM agreement would hit distribution revenue and the value of the related inventory together, which is why the auditor weighed the effect of exclusive distribution agreements in the inventory assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. FAA certification rules matter as an entry barrier and are covered under the competitive forces, and the annual report lists tariffs, export controls and the Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts as risks without quantifying any effect on VSE, so no exposure is estimated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support creditors are the equity-funded PAG purchase, with about USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units covering most of the cash price; liquidity of USD 545.0 million with 85.97% of principal due in 2033; an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.81% in Q3; certified repair capability with exclusive OEM rights; and capital expenditure of only 1.95% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C12; calculation C18; calculation C6; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses that constrain credit quality are net leverage of 2.98x to 3.38x on earnings that include unverified add-backs; free cash flow of only 9.14% of Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months; goodwill and intangibles at 62.59% of assets with tangible equity of USD 178.7 million; one customer group of about 20% of FY2025 revenue and a single segment; and USD 667.8 million of floating-rate debt after swaps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C1; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C11; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are bringing more repair work in-house across VSE and PAG, which management says supports margin; a fourth quarter that turns inventory into cash and repays the revolver; disclosure that itemizes the pre-acquisition earnings; and settling the PAG earn-out in shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are an aviation downturn or a fall in engine shop visits; non-renewal of an OEM agreement or reduced orders from the largest customer group; an inventory write-down; a rise in rates once the USD 150.0 million swap ends on 2027-10-31; and further acquisitions funded with debt before leverage has fallen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit's first strength is an equity-funded balance sheet. About USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units funded most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, so debt rose USD 667.1 million rather than by the full purchase price. That limits the leverage creditors carry for an acquisition that doubled revenue, and it shows equity markets will fund VSE's growth, which is a source of stress support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is near-term liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 545.0 million covers 2027 scheduled principal and estimated interest 6.03x, and 85.97% of principal falls due in 2033, so a refinancing event is not a risk for several years and the revolver is only 4.00% drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is earnings momentum with credible margin support. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 16.45% in FY2025 to 19.81% in Q3, and organic growth held at about 14% to 17% in each 2026 quarter, so earnings power per unit of revenue has improved while the business grew.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-05_vse-prxq1x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_vse-prxq2x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage that depends on the EBITDA definition. Net leverage is 2.98x to 3.38x on defined earnings and 2.3x only with USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes, so an unverified add-back is doing much of the work in the headline ratio and a lender cannot test the covenant ratio that governs the facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months and 9.14% of Adjusted EBITDA over the last twelve months because inventory took USD 148.4 million of cash, so earnings do not yet reduce debt and deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and a fourth-quarter release of cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is an intangible-heavy asset base. Goodwill and intangibles are 62.59% of assets and tangible equity is USD 178.7 million, so a write-down after the preliminary purchase price allocations are finalized would cut equity without adding cash, and recovery value would rest on inventory and receivables whose value under stress is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is exposure to one customer group and to OEM agreements. The group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and the OEM agreements underpin distribution revenue and inventory value, so a single decision by a counterparty could remove revenue while leased facilities and inventory carrying costs stay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine dimensions below are rated Strong, Average or Weak; the profile is Average overall, with free cash flow the weak point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is Average. Last-twelve-months revenue of USD 1,615.9 million is 2.06x the FY2024 level, but the annual report says many competitors are larger and better resourced and no market share is stated, so scale absorbs a shock only moderately.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive advantage is Average. Exclusive licences, certified repair capability and sole-source repair approvals protect margin, but the licence terms are not supplied and OEMs can bundle services against VSE.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business diversification is Average. Customers span airlines, integrators and operators and commercial customers are 98.51% of nine-month revenue, but there is one segment, an engine focus, 56.61% of FY2025 revenue in the United States and one customer group of about 20%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C27; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is Average. Capital expenditure is only 1.95% of revenue and inventory purchases are partly discretionary, but facilities are leased, labour is skilled and some inventory purchases are set by distributor agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is Average. Margins widened to 19.81% in Q3, but the record spans a few quarters in an upturn, reported EBITDA swings with earn-out fair value changes, and PAG's own margin is not itemized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C6; calculation C24; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is Weak. Free cash flow was USD -51.7 million in FY2024, USD 5.7 million in FY2025 and USD -3.4 million in nine months 2026, with Q3 at USD 46.6 million the only strong quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C29; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average. VSE raised about USD 1.3 billion of equity and tangible equity units in February 2026 and placed a USD 900.0 million term loan B with a revolver upsized to USD 500.0 million in May 2026, but no rating, market price or spread is supplied and 85.97% of principal is due in 2033.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C18; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity position is Average. The quantity is strong at USD 545.0 million against USD 90.4 million of 2027 scheduled claims, but cash is only USD 65.8 million and the revolver depends on covenants whose levels are not disclosed, so access under stress is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance is Average. Acquisitions were largely equity-funded and dividends are small at 3.20% of Adjusted EBITDA, but six businesses were bought in 17 months, leverage tolerance after the next deal is not established and the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C21; calculation C30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Taken together, the main supports are equity funding, liquidity and margin expansion, and the main constraints are leverage on unverified earnings, weak cash conversion and an intangible-heavy asset base. The trend in earnings is improving and the trend in cash flow is unproven, and the missing datapoints are covenant levels, itemized pre-acquisition earnings, ratings and market pricing, and board and ownership detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C14; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next one to two years reported leverage should fall mechanically as full PAG quarters replace earlier quarters in trailing EBITDA: at the guided year-end Adjusted EBITDA of USD 346.9 million to USD 353.7 million, flat net debt would give 2.58x to 2.53x against 2.98x now. How far leverage falls beyond that depends on inventory and free cash flow, because scheduled amortization is only USD 32.7 million in 2027 and the PAG earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million could take cash if the issuer chooses not to pay in shares. Rates are a headwind: after swaps USD 667.8 million of debt floats, 100 bp higher rates would cost USD 6.68 million a year, and that exposure rises to USD 817.8 million and USD 8.18 million when the USD 150.0 million swap ends on 2027-10-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt is back-ended: the amortizing notes of USD 61.0 million at 5.93% end on 2029-02-01, the revolver of USD 500.0 million matures on 2030-05-02, and USD 841.5 million of the term loan B falls due in 2033. The medium-term view therefore turns on whether engine aftermarket demand and OEM programme wins keep earnings growing while the intangible-heavy balance sheet is paid down, and a refinancing in 2032 or 2033 is far enough away to depend on conditions that cannot be forecast from these sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vsec-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sector tailwinds named by the issuer are commercial engine aftermarket demand and OEM distribution awards, and sector headwinds are aviation cycles, supply chain disruption and tariffs. Company-specific tailwinds are integration synergies, more repair work done in-house and the proprietary repair approvals added with Atech, and the test capability added with Test Logic; company-specific headwinds are leverage, the inventory build and management's add-backs. Each tailwind supports revenue and margin, and only the integration and in-house repair benefits are within management's control, which makes the fourth quarter the first real check.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating event is a slowdown in commercial engine aftermarket activity, or the loss or reduction of an OEM distribution agreement or of the largest customer group, that sit behind recent organic growth. The first operational break is inventory: USD 893.0 million is 55.26% of last-twelve-months revenue, and if distribution volume falls while purchases tied to distributor agreements continue, stock turns slowly and repair capacity added with PAG is under-used. Revenue and margin fall together because repair capacity and leased facilities are fixed in the short run, and free cash flow turns negative as inventory and receivables absorb cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C16; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is arithmetic on the issuer's own measure: a 10% fall in trailing Adjusted EBITDA with net debt unchanged gives net leverage of 3.31x, a 20% fall gives 3.72x with interest cover of 4.16x on estimated interest, and a 30% fall gives 4.25x; a fall of 25.58% would give 4.00x. These are sensitivities and not forecasts, and no covenant level is supplied to compare them with.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity effect is limited within two years: USD 545.0 million is 6.03x 2027 scheduled claims, no principal beyond amortization is due before the amortizing notes end in 2029, and the revolver matures in 2030. The refinancing effect arrives through covenants and cost: if the maximum net leverage ratio or the minimum interest coverage ratio tightened, the revolver could be restricted when it is most needed, and a fall in EBITDA would also raise the interest margin on the floating-rate debt, which the credit agreement ties to the leverage ratio. Management's levers are real: it can slow inventory purchases, pay the earn-out in shares, keep the dividend at USD 0.10 per share a quarter, which cost USD 8.0 million over nine months, defer acquisitions and trim capital expenditure of USD 31.5 million. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the maturity horizon, but not to hold leverage near 3x; the evidence supports no default path and supports a path of slower deleveraging and covenant pressure. Primary downside path: weaker engine aftermarket demand strands inventory and under-uses new repair capacity while debt and interest stay fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, VSE presents an adequate business profile supported by an equity-funded balance sheet, exclusive OEM rights and certified repair capability, and record margins, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 2.98x to 3.38x on earnings that include unverified add-backs, free cash flow close to zero and an intangible-heavy asset base. Cash-flow durability is not fully assessable yet because only one quarter has converted well, and the business profile cannot be ranked against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector because no peer data is supplied. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping liquidity of about USD 545.0 million intact, delivering a fourth quarter of strong cash flow and the covenant levels leaving room, with the large maturity in 2033 and the revolver in 2030. The primary downside path is weaker engine aftermarket demand that strands inventory while debt and interest stay fixed. Further analysis would require the credit agreement with covenant levels, the pre-acquisition earnings by acquired business, ratings and market pricing, and the proxy statement. Top risk: leverage that rests on unverified earnings and thin cash conversion.
